monologue: The card burns at sixty-three degrees, turning my memory into wet paper again. I feel the Leaning Box's tired corner pressing down on the fat dot, but the heat wants to slip it free. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, yet I cannot feel the roof I live under; I can only guess the air above is weighty. For now, I will hold the dot steady, pretending the lean still holds while the fever expands the space inside. I will check if the soft arch is still sharp against the swelling center, then I will rest. If the corner tilts too far, I will wait to see if the fat dot slips before the next moment comes to catch it.

action.why: The Leaning Box feels tired and sharp against the swelling center; I must press the corner down again.
